jaakan.s: (he shall adorn, or one sagacious), the son of Seir the Horite. Deut 10:6. See Bene-jaakan. The name is given as Jakan in 1 Chron 1:42.
He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).
(he shall surround), the same as Jakan, the forefather of Bene-Jaakan. (10:6)

jaakobah.s: ja-a-ko'-ba, ja-ak'-o-ba (ya`aqobhah, for meaning compare JACOB, I, 1, 2): 1Ch 4:36, a Simeonite prince.
(supplanter), one of the princes of the families of Simeon. (1 Chronicles 4:36) (B.C. about 710.)
Heel-catcher, a form of the name Jacob, one of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).
(heel catcher, supplanter), a chieftain of Simeon. 1 Chr 4:36.

jaala.s: (wild she-goat). Bene-Jaala were among the descendants of “Solomon’s slaves” who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel. (Nehemiah 7:58) (B.C. before 536.) The name also occurs as Ja-alah.
A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

jaalam.s: (whom God. hides), a son of Esau by his wife Aholibamah, and a chief of Edom. Gen 36:5, Gen 36:14, Gen 36:18; 1 Chr 1:35.
(whom God hides), a son of Esau, (Genesis 36:5,14,18) comp. 1Chr 1:35 And a head of a tribe of Edom. (B.C. 1790.).
Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).
ja'-a-lam: the King James Version for JALAM (which see).

jaanai.s: (whom Jehovah answers), a chief man in the tribe of Gad. (1 Chronicles 5:12)
ja'-a-ni: the King James Version for JANAI (which see).
(whom Jehovah answers), a chief of Gad. 1 Chr 5:12.
Mourner, one of the chief Gadites (1 Chr. 5:12).

jaare-oregim.s: ja'-a-re-or'-e-jim, -or'e-gim (ya`are'oreghim): In 2Sa 21:19, given as the name of a Bethlehemite, father of Elhanan, who is said to have slain Goliath the Gittite (compare 1Sa 17).
(forests of the weavers), the Bethlehemite whose son Elhanan slew the brother of Goliath. 2 Sam 21:19. In 1 Chr 20:5 he appears as Jair.
Forests of the weavers, a Bethlehemite (2 Sam. 21:19), and the father of Elhanan, who slew Goliath. In 1 Chr. 20:5 called JAIR.

jaasau.s: (whom Jehovah made), one of the Bene-Bani who had married a foreign wife. (Ezra 10:37) (B.C. 459.)
Fabricator, an Israelite who renounced his Gentile wife after the Return (Ezra 10:37).
(whom Jehovah has made), one mentioned, Ezr 10:37, as having a foreign wife.

jaasiel.s: ja-a'-si-el (ya`asi'el, "God makes" (?)): In 1Ch 11:47, a Mezobaite, one of "the mighty men of the armies," and probably = "Jaasiel" of 1Ch 27:21, "the son of Abner," and a Benjamite tribal prince of David's. the King James Version "Jasiel."
Made by God, one of David’s body-guard, the son of Abner (1 Chr. 27:21), called Jasiel in 1 Chr. 11:47.
(whom God has made), the son of Abner, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin. 1 Chr 27:21.
(whom God comforts), son of the great Abner. (1 Chronicles 27:21) (B.C. 1046-1014.)

jaaz-aniah.s: Heard by Jehovah. (1.) The son of Jeremiah, and one of the chief Rechabites (Jer. 35:3). (2.) The son of Shaphan (Ezek. 8:11). (3.) The son of Azur, one of the twenty-five men seen by Ezekiel (11:1) at the east gate of the temple. (4.) A Maachathite (2 Kings…

jaazer.s: and JA'ZER (Jehovah helps), a city of Gilead, east of the Jordan, which was conquered and assigned to Gad and to the Levites.
He (God) helps, a city of the Amorites on the east of Jordan, and assigned, with neighbouring places in Gilead, to Gad (Num.

jaaziah.s: (whom Jehovah comforts), apparently a third son, or a descendant, or Merari the Levite. (1 Chronicles 24:26,27) (B.C. before 1014).
ja-a-zi'-a (ya`aziyahu, "Yah strengthens"): In 1Ch 24:26,27, a Levite, "son" of Merari.
Comforted by Jehovah, a descendant of Merari the Levite (1 Chr. 24:26, 27).
(whom Jehovah consoles), a Levite of the family of Merari. 1 Chr 24:26-27.

jaaziel.s: ja-a'-zi-el (ya`azi'el, "God strengthens"): In 1Ch 15:18, a Levite, one of the musicians appointed to play upon instruments at the bringing up of the ark by David.
(whom Jehovah comforts), one of the Levites appointed by David to perform the musical service before the ark. (1 Chronicles 15:18) (B.C. 1014).
(whom God consoles), a Levite who played before the ark. 1 Chr 15:18. In 1 Chr 15:20 he is called Aziel.
Comforted by God, a Levitical musician (1 Chr. 15:18).

jabal.s: ja'-bal (yabhal, meaning uncertain): In Ge 4:20, a son of Lamech by Adah. He is called `the father of those who dwell in tents and (with) herds.' So Gunkel, Gen3, 52, who says that the corresponding word in Arabic means "the herdsman who tends the camels."…
A stream, a descendant of Cain, and brother of Jubal; “the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle” (Gen. 4:20). This description indicates that he led a wandering life.
(stream), the son of Lamech and Adah, (Genesis 4:20) and brother of Jubal. He is described as the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle.
(a stream), the son of Lamech, descendant of Cain; described as the "father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle." Gen 4:20.

jabbok.s: (emptying), a stream which intersects the mountain range of Gilead, comp. (Joshua 12:2,5) and falls into the Jordan on the east about midway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea. It was anciently the border of the children of Ammon. (Numbers 21:24;…

(emptying), a stream rising about 25 miles east of the north end of the Dead Sea, and flowing east, then northward and westward, and finally south-west, into the Jordan about midway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea.
jab'-ok (yabboq, "luxuriant river"): A stream in Eastern Palestine first named in the history of Jacob, as crossed by the patriarch on his return from Paddan-aram, after leaving Mahanaim (Ge 32:22).
A pouring out, or a wrestling, one of the streams on the east of Jordan, into which it falls about midway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, or about 45 miles below the Sea of Galilee.

jabesh.s: and JA'BESH-GIL'EAD (dry Gilead), a city east of the Jordan; destroyed by the Israelites, Jud 21:8-14; delivered from Nahash by Saul, 1 Sam 11:1-11, and in gratitude therefor its people brought the bodies of Saul and his sons, which the Philistines hung upon…

(dry). Father of Shallum, the fifteenth king of Israel. (2 Kings 15:10,13,14) Jabesh-gilead, or Jabesh in the territory of Gilead. In its widest sense Gilead included the half tribe of Manasseh, (1 Chronicles 27:21) as well as the tribes of Gad and Reuben,…
Dry. (1.) For Jabesh-Gilead (1 Sam. 11:3, 9, 10). (2.) The father of Shallum (2 Kings 15:10, 13, 14), who usurped the throne of Israel on the death of Zachariah.
(dry), the father of Shallum, the fifteenth king of Israel. 2 Kgs 15:10, 2 Kgs 15:13-14.
ja'-besh (yabhesh): A short form of JABESH-GILEAD (which see).

jabesh-gilead.s: ja'-besh-gil'-e-ad (yabhesh gil`adh; or simply yabhish, "dry"): A city East of the Jordan, in the deliverance of which from Nahash the Ammonite Saul's military prowess was first displayed (1Sa 11:1). At an earlier time the inhabitants failed to share with…
A town on the east of Jordan, on the top of one of the green hills of Gilead, within the limits of the half tribe of Manasseh, and in full view of Beth-shan.

jabez.s: (sorrow). Apparently a place at which the families of the scribes resided who belonged to the families of the Kenites. (1 Chronicles 2:55) The name occurs again in the genealogies of Judah, (1 Chronicles 4:9,10) in a passage of remarkable detail inserted in a…
Affiction. (1.) A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10). (2.) A place inhabited by several families of the scribes (1 Chr. 2:55).
(he causes pain), apparently a place; named only in 1 Chr 2:55, and doubtless named from Jabez of 1 Chr 4:9-10, though the Targumist regards it not as the name of a place, but of a person.
ja'-bez (ya`bets, "sorrow" ("height)): (1) Place: An unidentified town probably in the territory of Judah, occupied by scribes (1Ch 2:55).
(he causes pain), the name of one whose prayer was answered. 1 Chr 4:9-10.

jabin.s: Discerner; the wise. (1.) A king of Hazor, at the time of the entrance of Israel into Canaan (Josh. 11:1-14), whose overthrow and that of the northern chief with whom he had entered into a confederacy against Joshua was the crowning act in the conquest of the…

(whom God observes). King of Hazor, who organized a confederacy of the northern princes against the Israelites. (Joshua 11:1-3) Joshua surprised the allied forces by the waters of Merom, ver. 7, and utterly routed them. (B.C. 1448.) During the ensuing wars…
ja'-bin (yabhin, "one who is intelligent," "discerning." The word may have been a hereditary royal title among the northern Canaanites.

jabneel.s: Built by God. (1.) A town in the north boundary of Judah (Josh. 15:11), called afterwards by the Greeks Jamnia, the modern Yebna, 11 miles south of Jaffa. After the fall of Jerusalem (A.D. 70), it became one of the most populous cities of Judea, and the seat…

(building of God). One of the points on the northern boundary of Judah, not quite at the sea, though near it. (Joshua 15:11) There is no sign, however, of its ever having been occupied by Judah. Josephus attributes it to the Danites. There was a constant…

jachan.s: (affliction), one of seven chief men of the tribe of Gad. (1 Chronicles 5:13)
Mourner, one of the chief Gadite “brothers” in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

jachin.s: ja'-kin (yakhin, "he will establish"): (1) The 4th son of Simeon (Ge 46:10; Ex 6:15; Nu 26:12). In 1Ch 4:24 his name is given as "Jarib" (compare the King James Version margin, the Revised Version margin). "Jachinites," the patronymic of the family, occurs in…

(he shall establish). One of the two pillars which were set up “in the porch,” (1 Kings 7:21) or before the temple. (2 Chronicles 3:17) of Solomon. [Boaz] Fourth son of Simeon, (Genesis 46:10; Exodus 6:15) founder of the family of the Jachinites. (Numbers…

Firm. (1.) The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24). (2.) The head of one of the courses (the twenty-first) of priests (1 Chr. 24:17). (3.) One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).
(he shall establish) and BOAZ (lively) were the names of the two pillars Solomon set up. They were probably named after the givers. See Boaz.

jachin and boaz.s: ja'-kin (yakhin, "he shall establish"; bo`az, "in it is strength," 1Ki 7:15-22; 2Ki 25:16,17; 2Ch 3:15-17; Jer 52:17): These were the names of the two bronze pillars that stood before the temple of Solomon. They were not used in supporting the building; their…

The names of two brazen columns set up in Solomon’s temple (1 Kings 7:15-22). Each was eighteen cubits high and twelve in circumference (Jer. 52:21, 23; 1 Kings 7:17-21). They had doubtless a symbolical import.

jacinth.s: or HY'ACINTH, probably the same as the ligure, Ex 28:19, a gem of a yellowish-red or a dark-purple color, resembling the amethyst. Rev 9:17; Rev 21:20. In the former passage there is reference merely to its color.
Properly a flower of a reddish blue or deep purple (hyacinth), and hence a precious stone of that colour (Rev.
a precious stone, forming one of the foundations of the walls of the new Jerusalem.

jacob.s: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old. Like his…

(supplanter), the second son of Isaac and Rebekah. He was born with Esau, probably at the well of Lahai-roi, about B.C. 1837. His history is related in the latter half of the book of Genesis. He bought the birthright from his brother Esau, and afterward…
(heel-catcher, supplanter), the third of the Jewish patriarchs, the son of Isaac and Rebekah, and twin brother to Esau.

jacob’s well.s: (John 4:5, 6). This is one of the few sites in Palestine about which there is no dispute. It was dug by Jacob, and hence its name, in the “parcel of ground” which he purchased from the sons of Hamor (Gen. 33:19). It still exists, but although after copious…

jaddua.s: (known). Son and successor in the high priesthood of Jonathan or Johanan. He is the last of the high priests mentioned in the Old Testament, and probably altogether the latest name in the canon. (Nehemiah 12:11,22) (B.C. 406-332.) One of the chief of the…

jad'-u-a, ja-du'-a (yaddua`, "known"): (1) One of the "chiefs of the people" who with Nehemiah sealed the covenant, thus signifying their voluntary acceptance of the law and their solemn promise to submit to its yoke (Ne 10:21 (Hebrew 22)).
Known. (1.) One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:21). (2.) The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

jadon.s: ja'-don (yadhon, perhaps "he will judge" or "plead"): One who helped to rebuild the wall of Jerusalem in company with the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah (Ne 3:7).
(judge), the Meronothite, who assisted to repair the wall of Jerusalem. (Nehemiah 3:7) (B.C. 446.)
Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).
(judge), one who helped build the wall of Jerusalem. Neh 3:7.

jael.s: (mountain-goat), the wife of Heber the Kenite. Jud 4:17. After the defeat of Jabin's army by Deborah and Barak, Sisera, the general, fled toward her tent, because Heber and Jabin were at peace. It was not unusual for the women to have a tent separate from the…

ja'-el (ya`el, "a wild or mountain goat," as in Ps 104:18; Iael): The wife of Heber the Kenite and the slayer of Sisera (Jud 4:17-22; 5:2-31). Jael emerges from obscurity by this single deed, and by the kindest construction can hardly be said to have reached…

Mountain-goat, the wife of Heber the Kenite (Judg. 4:17-22). When the Canaanites were defeated by Barak, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, fled and sought refuge with the friendly tribe of Heber, beneath the oaks of Zaanaim. As he drew near, Jael invited…

(mountain goat), the wife of Heber the Kenite. (B.C. 1316.) In the headlong rout which followed the defeat of the Canaanites by Barak, at Megiddo on the plain of Esdraelon, Sisera, their general, fled to the tent of the Kenite chieftainess, at Kedesh in…

jagur.s: a city on the south-eastern frontier of Judah, near Edom, Josh 15:21; perhaps to be associated with the following word. See Kinah.
(lodging), a town of Judah, one of those farthest to the south, on the frontier of Edom. (Joshua 15:21)
ja'-gur (yaghur): An unidentified town on the Edomite frontier of Judah in the South (Jos 15:21).
Place of sojourn, a city on the southern border of Judah (Josh. 15:21).

jah.s: (Jehovah), the abbreviated form of Jehovah, used only in poetry. It occurs frequently in the Hebrew, but with a single exception, (Psalms 68:4) is rendered “Lord” in the Authorized Version. The identity of Jah and Jehovah is strongly marked in two passages of…

Ps 68:4. A contraction of the word "Jehovah," which imports the attribute of self-existence. It is part of the compound words "Adonijah" ("God is my Lord") and "Hallelujah" ("Praise the Lord"). See Jehovah.

jahath.s: (union). Son of Libni, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi. (1 Chronicles 6:20) (B.C. after 1706.) Head of a later house in the family of Gershom, being the eldest son of Shimei, the son of Laadan. (1 Chronicles 23:10,11) A man in the genealogy of Judah, (1…

Union. (1.) A son of Shimei, and grandson of Gershom (1 Chr. 23:10). (2.) One of the sons of Shelomoth, of the family of Kohath (1 Chr. 24:22). (3.) A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the overseers of the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr.…

ja'-hath (yachath, perhaps for yachteh, yachatheh, "he (God) will snatch up"): (1) Son of Reaiah, son of Shobal, a descendant of Judah, and father of Ahumai and Lahad, the families of the Zorathites (1Ch 4:2).

jahaz.s: (place trodden down), a Moabitish city situated near the desert; afterward reckoned to the tribe of Reuben and assigned to the priests. Num 21:23; Deut 2:32; Isa 15:4; Jer 48:34. It is also called Jahaza, Josh 13:18, Jahazah, Josh 21:36; Jer 48:21, and Jahzah.…

Trodden down (called also Jahaza, Josh. 13:18; Jahazah, 21:36; Jahzah, 1 Chr. 6:78), a town where Sihon was defeated, in the borders of Moab and in the land of the Ammonites beyond Jordan, and north of the river Arnon (Num. 21:23; Deut. 2:32). It was situated…

ja'-haz (yahats, Isa 16:4; Jer 48:34, yahatsah, or yahtsah, Nu 21:23; De 2:32; Jos 13:18; 21:36, the King James Version "Jahazah"; Jud 11:20; Jer 48:21; 1Ch 6:78, "Jahzah"): This is the place where in a great battle Israel overwhelmed Sihon king of the…

jahaziel.s: Beheld by God. (1.) The third son of Hebron (1 Chr. 23:19). (2.) A Benjamite chief who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4). (3.) A priest who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:6). (4.) The son of Zechariah, a Levite of the family of…

(whom God watches over) One of the heroes of Benjamin who joined David at Ziklag. (1 Chronicles 12:4) (B.C. 1055.) A priest in the reign of David. (1 Chronicles 16:6) A Kohathite Levite, third son of Hebron. (1 Chronicles 23:19; 24:23) Son of Zechariah, a…
ja-ha'-zi-el (yachazi'el, "God sees"): (1) In 1Ch 12:4 (Hebrew 5), one of David's recruits at Ziklag, a Benjamite or maybe a Judean.

jahdai.s: ja'-da-i, ja'-di (yahday, "Yah leads" (?); Baer reads yehday): In 1Ch 2:47, where six sons of Jahdai are mentioned. "The name has been taken as that of another wife or concubine of Caleb; more probably Jahdai is a descendant of Caleb, whose name, in the…
(whom Jehovah directs), a man who appears to be thrust abruptly into the genealogy of Caleb, as the father of six sons. (1 Chronicles 2:47)
(whom Jehovah directs), a name in the genealogies of Judah. 1 Chr 2:47.
Grasper, a descendant of Caleb, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:47).

jahzeel.s: (whom God allots), the first of the four sons of Naphtali, (Genesis 46:24) founder of the family of the Jahzeelites. (Numbers 26:48) (B.C. 1306.)
(whom God allots), the eldest son of Naphtali, and founder of the Jahzeelites. Gen 46:24; 1 Chr 7:13.
Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

jahzerah.s: ja'-ze-ra, ja-ze'-ra (yachzerah, meaning unknown): In 1Ch 9:12, an ancestor of Maasai and apparently = "Ahzai" of Ne 11:13.
(whom God leads back), a priest of the house of Immer, 1 Chr 9:12; called Ahasai in the duplicate passage in Neh 11:13.
(whom God leads back), a priest of the house of Immer. (1 Chronicles 9:12)
Returner, the son of Meshullam, and father of Adiel (1 Chr. 9:12).

jailer.s: (of Philippi), Acts 16:23. The conversion of the Roman jailer, a man belonging to a class “insensible as a rule and hardened by habit, and also disposed to despise the Jews, who were the bearers of the message of the gospel,” is one of those cases which…

jair.s: Enlightener. (1.) The son of Segub. He was brought up with his mother in Gilead, where he had possessions (1 Chr. 2:22). He distinguished himself in an expedition against Bashan, and settled in the part of Argob on the borders of Gilead. The small towns taken…

ja'-er: (1) Jair (ya'ir, "he enlightens" or "one giving light"): (a) Son, i.e. descendant of Manasseh (Nu 32:41; De 3:14; Jos 13:30; 1Ki 4:13; 1Ch 2:22 f). According to 1Ch 2:21 f he was the son of ScRub, son of Hezron, a descendant of Judah, who married the…

(enlightener). A man who on his father’s side was descended from Judah, and on his mother’s from Manasseh. (B.C. 1451.) During, the conquest he took the whole of the tract of Argob (3:14) and in addition possessed himself of some nomad villages in Gilead,…

jairus.s: (whom God enlightens). A ruler of a synagogue, probably in some town near the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. (Matthew 9:18; Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41) (A.D. 28.) (Esther 11:2) [Jair, 3]
(whom Jehovah enlightens), an officer of the Jewish church who applied to Christ to restore to life his daughter, who was at the point of death when he left home.
A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22;

jakeh.s: ja'-ke (yaqeh, perhaps from Arabic root meaning "carefully religious"; yaqe', as if from qi'): The father of Agur, the author of the sayings recorded in Pr 30:1. Nothing is known of either Jakeh or Agur. The immediate connection in the Hebrew text of…
(pious), the father of Agur, whose "words" are recorded in Prov 30.
Pious, the father of Agur (Prov. 30:1). Nothing is known of him.

jakim.s: ja'-kim (yaqim, "he (God) lifteth Up"; compare ELIAKIM): (1) A Benjamite, a son of Shimei (1Ch 8:19). (2) A priest, the head of the 12th of the 24 courses into which the priests were divided (1Ch 24:12).
(whom God sets up). Head of the twelfth course of priests in the reign of David. (1 Chronicles 24:12) (B.C. 1014.) A Benjamite, one of the Bene-Shimhi. (1 Chronicles 8:19) (B.C. 588.)
Establisher. (1.) Chief of the twelfth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:12). (2.) A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:19). (3.) Margin in Matt. 1:11 means Jehoiakim.

jalon.s: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).
ja'-lon (yalon, meaning unknown): In 1Ch 4:17, a son of Ezrah, a Judahite.
(abiding), one of the sons of Ezra. (1 Chronicles 4:17)

jambres.s: One of those who opposed Moses in Egypt (2 Tim. 3:8). (See JANNES.)

james.s: (the Greek form of Jacob, supplanter). James the son of Zebedee, one of the twelve apostles. He was elder brother of the evangelist John. His mother’s name was Salome. We first hear of him in A.D. 27, (Mark 1:20) when at the call of the Master he left all, and…

(1.) The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56). With John and Peter he was present at the transfiguration (Matt. 17:1; Mark 9:2),…
jamz (Iacobos): English form of Jacob, and the name of 3 New Testament men of note: (1) The Son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve Apostles (ho tou Zebedaiou): A) The Son of Zebedee: I.

james, epistle of.s: || I. CHARACTERISTICS OF THE EPISTLE 1. Jewish 2. Authoritative 3. Practical II. AUTHOR OF THE EPISTLE III. STYLE OF THE EPISTLE 1. Plainness 2. Good Greek 3. Vividness 4. Duadiplosis 5. Figures of Speech 6. Unlikeness to Paul 7. Likeness to Jesus IV. DATE OF…
(1.) Author of, was James the Less, the Lord’s brother, one of the twelve apostles.

jannes.s: and JAM'BRES, two famous magicians of Egypt, who are supposed to have used their art to deceive Pharaoh. 2 Tim 3:8; Ex 7:9-13.
and Jam’bres, the names of two Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses. Exod 7:9-13; 2Tim 3:8,9. (B.C. 1492.)
One of the Egyptians who “withstood Moses” (2 Tim. 3:8).

janoah.s: (rest), a town of Naphtali, in northern Palestine, taken by the king of Assyria. 2 Kgs 15:29. Van de Velde and Porter propose to identify it with ruins at the village Hunis, between Abel-beth-Maachah and Kedesh; Conder with Yanuk, near the western limit of the…

Or Jano’hah, rest. (1.) A town on the north-eastern border of Ephraim, in the Jordan valley (Josh. 16:6, 7). Identified with the modern Yanun, 8 miles south-east of Nablus. (2.) A town of Northern Palestine, within the boundaries of Naphtali. It was taken by…

(rest), a place apparently in the north of Galilee, or the “land of Naphtali,”—one of those taken by Tiglath-pileser in his first incursion into Palestine. (2 Kings 15:29) No trace of it appears elsewhere.
ja-no'-a (yanoach, "resting-place"): (1) A place named on the eastern boundary of Ephraim (Jos 16:6 f;

janum.s: (slumber), a place in the tribe of Judah. Josh 15:53. The margin has "Janus" ("flight"). It was not far from Hebron, and Conder proposes to identify it with Beni Naim.
(slumber), a town of Judah in the mountain district, apparently not far from Hebron. (Joshua 15:53)
Slumber, a town in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:53).
ja'-num (Qere, yanum, Kethibh yanim). See JANIM.

japheth.s: Wide spreading: “God shall enlarge Japheth” (Heb. Yaphat Elohim le-Yephet, Gen. 9:27. Some, however, derive the name from yaphah, “to be beautiful;” hence white), one of the sons of Noah, mentioned last in order (Gen. 5:32; 6:10; 7:13), perhaps first by birth…

(enlargement), one of the three sons of Noah. The descendants of Japheth occupied the “isles of the Gentiles,” (Genesis 10:5)—i.e. the coast lands of the Mediterranean Sea in Europe and Asia Minor— whence they spread northward over the whole continent of…

(enlargement), the second son of Noah. Gen 5:32; Gen 10:21. The prophetic blessing pronounced on Japheth by his father, Gen 9:27, was accomplished to the full extent of the promise. From him have come, (1) Gomer, or the Cymri or Celts; (2) Magog, or the…

japhia.s: (splendid). King of Lachish at the time of the conquest of Canaan by the Israelites. (Joshua 10:3) (B.C. 1450.) One of the sons of David born to him in Jerusalem. (2 Samuel 5:15; 1 Chronicles 3:7; 14:6) (B.C. 1046.) (splended) The boundary of Zebulun ascended…

Splendid. (1.) The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Josh. 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Josh. 10:33). (2.) One of the sons of David (2…

(splendid), a place in the tribe of Zebulun. Josh 19:12. It is identified with a small village, called Yafa, a short distance south-west of Nazareth. See Josephus: Wars, 2:20, 6. Drake described some caves at this place unlike any other he had seen in…
(splendid), the king of Lachish, one of the five kings of the Amorites who united against Joshua, but were defeated at Beth-horon and killed at Makkedah. Josh 10:3.

japho.s: (beauty). (John 19:46) The Hebrew form for the better-known Joppa, Or Japho. (2 Chronicles 2:16; Ezra 3:7; Jonah 1:3) In its modern garb it is Yafa .
Beauty, a sea-port in Dan (Josh. 19:46); called Joppa (q.v.) in 2 Chr. 2:16; Ezra 3:7; Jonah 1:3; and in New Testament.
ja'-fo: the King James Version and the American Revised Version margin in Jos 19:46 for JOPPA (which see).

jared.s: ja'-red (yeredh, "descent"; pausal form, yaredh, in Ge 5:15; 1Ch 1:2, hence, English Versions of the Bible "Jared" for "Jered"; Iared): In Ge 5:15-20; 1Ch 1:2; Lu 3:37, son of Mahalaleel and father of Enoch. The King James Version has "Jered" in 1Ch 1:2. The…
Descent. (1.) The fourth antediluvian patriarch in descent from Seth (Gen. 5:15-20; Luke 3:37), the father of Enoch; called Jered in 1 Chr. 1:2. (2.) A son of Ezra probably (1 Chr. 4:18).
(descent), one of the antediluvian patriarchs, and further of Enoch (Genesis 5:15,16,18-20; Luke 3:37) In the lists of Chronicles the name is given in the Authorized Version Jered.
(descent), the father of Enoch. Gen 5:15-20; Luke 3:37. In 1 Chr 1:2 he is called Jered.

jarib.s: (adversary). Named in the list of (1 Chronicles 4:24) only, as a son of Simeon. Perhaps the same as Jachin. Genesis46; Exod 6; Numb 26. One of the “chief men” who accompanied Ezra on his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem. (Ezra 8:16) (B.C. 469.) A priest of…
ja'-rib, jar'-ib (yaribh, "he contends," or "takes (our) part," or "conducts (our) case"): (1) In 1Ch 4:24, a "son" (clan) of Simeon = "Jachin" of Ge 46:10;
An adversary. (1.) A son of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:24). (2.) One of the chiefs sent by Ezra to bring up the priests to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16). (3.) Ezra 10:18.

jarmuth.s: (high). A town in the low country of Judah. (Joshua 16:35) Its king, Piram, was one of the five who conspired. to punish Gibeon for having made alliance with Israel, (Joshua 10:3,5) and who were routed at Beth-horon and put to death by Joshua at Makkedah. ver.…

1. A town in the low country of Judah. Josh 15:35. Its king, Piram, was one of the five who conspired to punish Gibeon for having made alliance with Israel, and who were defeated at Beth-horon and were hanged by Joshua at Makkedah. Josh 12:11; Josh 15:35. It…

Height. (1.) A town in the plain of Judah (Josh. 15:35), originally the residence of one of the Canaanitish kings (10:3, 5, 23). It has been identified with the modern Yarmuk, a village about 7 miles north-east of Beit-Jibrin. (2.) A Levitical city of the…

jar'-muth (yarmuth: (1) A city of the Canaanites in the Shephelah (Jos 15:35) of Judah whose "king," Piram, joined the league of the "five kings" against Joshua (Jos 10:3-5), was defeated at Gibeon and slain at Makkedah (10:23).

jashen.s: (sleeping). Bene-Jashen—“sons of Jashen”— are named in the catalogue of the heroes of David’s guard in (2 Samuel 23:32) (B.C. 1046.)
Sleeping, called also Hashem (1 Chr. 11:34); a person, several of whose sons were in David’s body-guard (2 Sam. 23:32).
ja'-shen, jash'-en (yashen, "asleep"(?)): Seemingly the father of some of David s thirty valiant men (2Sa 23:32 f).
(sleeping), the father of some of David's warriors, 2 Sam 23:32.

jasher.s: Upright. “The Book of Jasher,” rendered in the LXX. “the Book of the Upright One,” by the Vulgate “the Book of Just Ones,” was probably a kind of national sacred song-book, a collection of songs in praise of the heroes of Israel, a “book of golden deeds,” a…
(upright),Book of (“the book of the upright”), alluded to in two passages only of the Old Testament.

jashobeam.s: ja-sho'-be-am (yashobh`am, probably "people will return"; see discussion of names compounded with `am, in HPN, 41-59): Jashobeam is mentioned in three passages (1Ch 11:11; 12:6 (Hebrew 7); 27:2 f), but opinions vary as to the number of persons erred to. In 1Ch…

Dweller among the people; or to whom the people turn, the Hachmonite (1 Chr. 11:11), one of David’s chief heroes who joined him at Ziklag (12:6). He was the first of the three who broke through the host of the Philistines to fetch water to David from the well…

(to whom the people turn), named first among the chief of the mighty men of David. (1 Chronicles 11:11) (B.C. 1046.) He came to David at Ziklag. His distinguishing exploit was that he slew 300 (or 800,) (2 Samuel 23:8) men at one time.
(to whom the people turns), the chief of David's captains, who came to him at Ziklag and distinguished himself and his band by slaying 300 men at one time.

jashub.s: ja'-shub, jash'-ub (yashubh; yashibh, in Chronicles, but Qere, yashubh, "he returns"): (1) In Nu 26:24; 1Ch 7:1, a "son" (clan) of Issachar. Ge 46:13 has incorrectly Iob, but Septuagint Jashub. (2) In Ezr 10:29, one of those who had married foreign wives =…

(he turns). The third son of Issachar, and founder of the family of the Jashubites. (Numbers 26:24; 1 Chronicles 7:1) (B.C. 1706.) One of the sons of Bani, who had to put away his foreign wife. (Ezra 10:29) (B.C. 459.)
Returner. (1.) The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13). (2.) Ezra 10:29.

jason.s: He that will cure, the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica. The Jews assaulted his house in order to seize Paul, but failing to find him, they dragged Jason before the ruler of the city (Acts 17:5-9). He was apparently one of the kinsmen of Paul (Rom.…

(one who will heal), a Thessalonian, and probably a relative of Paul, whom he entertained, and in consequence received rough treatment at the hands of the unbelieving Jews. Acts 17; cf. Rom 9:3; Deut 16:21.
(one who will heal), called the Thessalonian, entertained Paul and Silas, and was in consequence attacked by the Jewish mob.

jasper.s: a precious stone frequently noticed in Scripture. It was the last of the twelve inserted in the high priest’s breastplate, (Exodus 28:20; 39:13) and the first of the twelve used in the foundations of the new Jerusalem. (Revelation 21:19) The characteristics of…

(Heb. yashpheh, “glittering”), a gem of various colours, one of the twelve inserted in the high priest’s breast-plate (Ex. 28:20). It is named in the building of the New Jerusalem (Rev. 21:18, 19). It was “most precious,” “clear as crystal” (21:11). It was…
the last stone in the breastplate of the high priest, and the first in the foundations of the new Jerusalem.

jattir.s: a town of Judah in the mountain-districts, Josh 15:48; 2 Sam 21:14; David sent presents thither. 1 Sam 30:27; 1 Chr 6:57. Robinson identifies it with 'Attir, 6 miles north of Molada and 11 miles west of south of Hebron. Tristram noted there over 30 crypts, and…
jat'-er (yattir, and yattir): A town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in conjunction with Shamir and Socoh (Jos 15:48);
(pre-eminent), a town of Judah in the mountain districts, (Joshua 15:48) one of the group containing Socho, Eshtemoa, etc.
Pre-eminent, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:48; 21:14).

javan.s: ja'-van (yawan, meaning unknown): (1) In Ge 10:2,4 = 1Ch 1:5,7 Septuagint Iouan); Isa 66:19; Eze 27:13 Septuagint Hellas, Greece); Da 8:21 m; 10:20; 11:2; Zec 9:13; Joe 3:6 (Hebrew 4:6) Septuagint hoi Hellenes, i.e. "Greeks"), "son" of Japheth, and "father" of…

(1.) The fourth “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew. Alexander the Great is called the “king of Javan” (rendered “Grecia,” Dan. 8:21; 10:20; comp. 11:2; Zech. 9:13). This word…

(clay). A son of Japheth. (Genesis 10:2,4) Javan was regarded as the representative of the Greek race. The name was probably introduced into Asia by the Phoenicians, to whom the Ionians were naturally better known than any other of the Hellenic races, on…
the fourth son of Japheth, and the ancestor of the Grecians or lonians. Gen 10:2; 1 Chr 1:5, 1 Chr 1:7. Hence the word "Javan" in the O.T. denotes Greece, or the Greeks. Isa 66:19; Eze 27:13.

javelin.s: (1.) Heb. hanith, a lance, from its flexibility (1 Sam. 18:10, 11; 19:9, 10; 20:33). (2.) Heb. romah, a lance for heavy-armed troops, so called from its piercing (Num. 25:7). (See ARMS.)

jaw-bone.s: Of an ass afforded Samson a weapon for the great slaughter of the Philistines (Judg.

jealousy.s: jel'-us-i (qin'ah; zelos): Doubtless, the root idea of both the Greek and the Hob translated "jealousy" is "warmth," "heat." Both are used in a good and a bad sense--to represent right and wrong passion. When jealousy is attributed to God, the word is used in…

It is most frequently used to denote a suspicion of conjugal infidelity. 2 Cor 11:2. It is sometimes used for anger or indignation, Ps 79:5; 1 Cor 10:22, or an intense interest for the honor and prosperity of another. Zech 1:14; Zech 8:2.
Suspicion of a wife’s purity, one of the strongest passions (Num. 5:14; Prov. 6:34; Cant. 8:6); also an intense interest for another’s honour or prosperity (Ps. 79:5; 1 Cor. 10:22; Zech. 1:14).

jealousy, image of.s: An idolatrous object, seen in vision by Ezekiel (Ezek. 8:3, 5), which stood in the priests’ or inner court of the temple. Probably identical with the statue of Astarte (2 Kings 21:7).

jealousy offering.s: The name of the offering the husband was to bring when he charged his wife with adultery (Num. 5:11-15).

jealousy, waters of.s: Water which the suspected wife was required to drink, so that the result might prove her guilt or innocence (Num. 5:12-17, 27). We have no record of this form of trial having been actually resorted to.

jearim.s: (forests), Mount, a place named in specifying the northern boundary of Judah. (Joshua 15:10) The boundary ran from Mount Seir to “the shoulder of Mount Jearim, which is Cesalon”—that is, Cesalon was the landmark on the mountain. Kesla, seven miles due west of…
Forests, a mountain on the border of Judah (Josh. 15:10).

jebus.s: je'-bus (yebhuc; Iebous): In Jud 19:10,11, "Jebus (the same is Jerusalem)"; 1Ch 11:4,5, "Jerusalem (the same is Jebus)." It was once thought that this was the first name of Jerusalem, as indeed might be suggested by the Biblical references, but it is now known…
(threshing-floor), one of the names of Jerusalem, the city of the Jebusites, are called Jebusi. (Joshua 15:8; 18:16,28; Judges 19:10,11; 1 Chronicles 11:4,5) [Jerusalem]
Trodden hard, or fastness, or “the waterless hill”, the name of the Canaanitish city which stood on Mount Zion (Josh.
(place trodden down, threshing- floor), the ancient name of Jerusalem among the Canaanites, Jud 19:10-11;

jebusites.s: (descendants of Jebus), The, were descended from the third son of Canaan. (Genesis 10:16; 1 Chronicles 1:14) The actual people first appear in the invaluable report of the spies. (Numbers 13:29) When Jabin organized his rising against Joshua, the Jebusites…
the name of a tribe inhabiting the portion of Canaan about Jebus or Jerusalem in the time of Joshua, and which the Israelites were commanded to destroy.
The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen.

jecoliah.s: Able through Jehovah, the wife of King Amaziah, and mother of King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:3).
jek-o-li'-a: 2Ki 15:2; 2Ch 26:3 the King James Version; see JECHILIAH; JECHOLIAH.

jedaiah.s: (1.) Invoker of Jehovah. The son of Shimri, a chief Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37). (2.) One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10). (3.) Knowing Jehovah. The chief of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:7).…

A Simeonite, forefather of Ziza. (1 Chronicles 4:37) Son of Harumaph; a man who did his part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem. (Nehemiah 3:10) (B.C. 446.) (praise Jehovah). Head of the second course of priests, as they were divided in the time of…
je-da'-ya, je-di'-a: (1) (yedha`yah, "Yah knows"): (a) A priest in Jerusalem (1Ch 9:10;

jediael.s: Known by God. (1.) One of the sons of Benjamin, whose descendants numbered 17,200 warriors (1 Chr. 7:6, 10, 11). (2.) A Shimrite, one of David’s bodyguard (1 Chr. 11:45). Probably same as in 12:20. (3.) A Korhite of the family of Ebiasaph, and one of the…

(known of God). A chief patriarch of the tribe of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 7:6,11) It is usually assumed that Jediael is the same as Ashbel, (Genesis 46:21; Numbers 26:38; 1 Chronicles 8:1) but this is not certain. Second son of Meshelemiah, a Levite. (1…
je-di'-a-el (yedhi`a'-el, "God makes known" (?)): (1) A "son" of Benjamin or probably of Zebulun (1Ch 7:6,10,11).

jedidiah.s: (beloved of Jehovah), the name Nathan gave to Solomon. 2 Sam 12:25. It was a play on the word David, "beloved," which comes from the same root as "Jedid;" so, as the father was beloved, the child was the beloved of Jehovah.
Beloved by Jehovah, the name which, by the mouth of Nathan, the Lord gave to Solomon at his birth as a token of the divine favour (2 Sam. 12:25).
(beloved of Jehovah), Jedid-jah (darling of Jehovah), the name bestowed, through Nathan the prophet, on David’s son Solomon. (2 Samuel 12:25)
jed-i-di'-a (yedhidh-yah, "the beloved of Yah"): The name conferred by God through Nathan upon Solomon at his birth (2Sa 12:25).

jeduthun.s: (praising), a Levite of the family of Merari, is probably the same as Ethan. Comp. (1 Chronicles 15:17,19) with 1Chr 16:41,42; 25:1,3,6; 2Chr 35:15 His office was generally to preside over the music of the temple service, Jeduthun’s name stands at the head of…

Lauder; praising, a Levite of the family of Merari, and one of the three masters of music appointed by David (1 Chr. 16:41, 42; 25:1-6). He is called in 2 Chr. 35:15 “the king’s seer.” His descendants are mentioned as singers and players on instruments (Neh.…
(praising), an eminent master of the temple-music, to whom several of the Psalms are inscribed, see Ps 39, Ps 62, Ps 77, etc., or by whom, as some suppose, they were written.

jegar-sahadutha.s: Pile of testimony, the Aramaic or Syriac name which Laban gave to the pile of stones erected as a memorial of the covenant between him and Jacob (Gen. 31:47), who, however, called it in Hebrew by an equivalent name, Galeed (q.v.).
(heap of testimony), the Aramaean name of the stone memorial between Jacob and Laban. Gen 31:47. The Hebrew word "Galeed" does not exactly represent it.

jehaleleel.s: (who praises God). Four men of the Bene-Jehaleleel are introduced abruptly into the genealogies of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:16)
Praiser of God. (1.) A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 4:16). (2.) A Levite of the family of Merari (2 Chr. 29:12).

jehdeiah.s: (whom Jehovah makes glad). The representative of the Bene-Shubael, in the time of David. (1 Chronicles 24:20) A Meronothite who had charge of the she-asses of David. (1 Chronicles 27:30) (B.C. 1046.)
Rejoicer in Jehovah. (1.) One of the Levitical attendants at the temple, a descendant of Shubael (1 Chr. 24:20). (2.) A Meronothite, herdsman of the asses under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:30).
je-de'-ya, ja'-de-ya (yechdeyahu, "may Yahweh give joy!"): (1) A Levite, head of the family of Shubael (1Ch 24:20). (2) An officer of David "over the asses" (1Ch 27:30).

jehiel.s: God’s living one. (1.) The father of Gibeon (1 Chr. 9:35). (2.) One of David’s guard (1 Chr. 11:44). (3.) One of the Levites “of the second degree,” appointed to conduct the music on the occasion of the ark’s being removed to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:18, 20). (4.)…

(treasured of God), a perfectly distinct name from the last. A man described as father of Gibeon; a fore-father of King Saul. (1 Chronicles 9:35) One of the sons of Hotham the Aroerite; a member of David’s guard. (1 Chronicles 11:44) (B.C. 1046.) (God lives).…
(God lives). 1. A Levite porter appointed by David for musical service. 1 Chr 15:18, 1 Chr 15:20; 1 Chr 16:5.
(treasured of God?), a distinct name in Hebrew from the last.

jehizkiah.s: je-hiz-ki'-a (yechizqiyahu, "Yah strengthens"): One of the Ephraimite chiefs (2Ch 28:12) who with Obed are said to have opposed the enslavement of the Judahites taken captive by Pekah in his war against Ahaz (circa 734 BC).
(whom Jehovah strengthens), the same name as Hezekiah. One of the Ephraimite chiefs who seconded the prophet Oded in his efforts to release the captives of Judah during Ahaz's reign. 2 Chr 28:12.
(Jehovah strengthens), son of Shallum, one of the heads of the tribe of Ephraim in the time of Ahaz. (2 Chronicles 28:12) comp. 2Chr 28:8,13,15 (B.C. 738.)
Jehovah strengthens, one of the chiefs of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12).

jehoaddan.s: je-ho-ad'-an (yeho`addan, meaning unknown): In 2Ch 25:1; and Qere, the King James Version in 2Ki 14:2, where Kethibh and the Revised Version (British and American) are "Jehoaddin" (yeho`addin), the mother of King Amaziah of Judah.
(the feminine form of the above), the queen of Joash and mother of Amaziah, the succeeding king of Judah. 2 Kgs 14:2; 2 Chr 25:1.
(Whom Jehovah adorns), queen to King Josiah, and mother of Amaziah of Judah. (2 Kings 14:2; 2 Chronicles 25:1) (B.C. 862-837.)
Jehovah his ornament, the wife of King Jehoash, and mother of King Amaziah (2 Kings 14:2).

jehoahaz.s: je-ho'-a-haz, je-ho-a'-haz (yeho'achaz, "Yah has grasped"; Ioachas; 2Ki 13:1-9): (1) Son of Jehu, and 11th king of Israel. He is stated to have reigned 17 years. 1. Chronology of Reign: Josephus was already aware (Ant., IX, viii, 5) of the chronological…

Jehovah his sustainer, or he whom Jehovah holdeth. (1.) The youngest son of Jehoram, king of Judah (2 Chr. 21:17; 22:1, 6, 8, 9); usually Ahaziah (q.v.). (2.) The son and successor of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 10:35). He reigned seventeen years, and…

(whom the Lord sustains). The son and successor of jehu, reigned 17 years, B.C. 856-840, over Israel in Samaria. His inglorious history is given in (2 Kings 13:1-9) Throughout his reign, ver. (2 Kings 13:22) he was kept in subjection by Hazael king of…

jehoash.s: Jehovah-given. (1.) The son of King Ahaziah. While yet an infant, he was saved from the general massacre of the family by his aunt Jehosheba, and was apparently the only surviving descendant of Solomon (2 Chr. 21:4, 17). His uncle, the high priest Jehoiada,…

(given by the Lord), the uncontracted form of Joash. The eighth king of Judah; son of Ahaziah. (2 Kings 11:21; 12:1,2,4,6,7,18; 14:13) [Joash, 1] The twelfth king of Israel; son of Jehoahaz. (2 Kings 13:10,25; 14:8,9,11,13,15,16,17) [Joash, 2]
(whom Jehovah bestowed), original uncontracted form of the name commonly written Joash, and applied to two kings. See Joash, 3 and 4.

jehohanan.s: (whom Jehovah gave), a name of which John is the contraction. A Korhite Levite, one of the doorkeepers to the tabernacle. (1 Chronicles 26:3) comp. 1Chr 25:1 (B.C. 1014.) One of the principal men of Judah under King Jehoshaphat. (2 Chronicles 17:15) comp. 2Chr…

Jehovah-granted, Jeroboam II. (1.) A Korhite, the head of one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:3). (2.) One of Jehoshaphat’s “captains” (2 Chr. 17:15). (3.) The father of Azariah (2 Chr. 28:12). (4.) The son of Tobiah, an enemy of the Jews…
je-ho-ha'-nan (yehochanan, "Yahweh is (or has been) gracious"): (1) A Korahite doorkeeper in David's reign, "son" of Meshelemiah (1Ch 26:3).
(whom Jehovah gave), a name contracted into Johanan, and thus into the familiar John.

jehoiachin.s: Succeeded his father Jehoiakin (B.C. 599) when only eight years of age, and reigned for one hundred days (2 Chr. 36:9). He is also called Jeconiah (Jer. 24:1; 27:20, etc.), and Coniah (22:24; 37:1). He was succeeded by his uncle, Mattaniah = Zedekiah (q.v.).…

je-hoi'-a-kin (yehoyakhin, "Yahweh will uphold"; called also "Jeconiah" in 1Ch 3:16; Jer 24:1; yekhonyah, "Yahweh will be steadfast," and "Coniah" in Jer 22:24,28; konyahu, "Yahweh has upheld him"; 'Ioakeim): A king of Judah; son and successor of Jehoiakim;…

(whom Jehovah has appointed). Jeconiah, 1 Chr 3:17; Coniah, Jer 22:24; Jeconias, Matt 1:12. Son and successor of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, b.c. 598. 2 Kgs 24:8. He was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and reigned only three months and ten days, at…
(whom Jehovah has appointed), son of Jehoiakim, and for three months and ten days king of Judah.

jehoiada.s: Jehovah-known. (1.) The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23). (2.) The high priest at the time of Athaliah’s usurpation of the throne of Judah. He married Jehosheba, or Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram (2 Chr.…

je-hoi'-a-da (yehoyadha`, "Yahweh knows"; Iodae): (1) Father of Benaiah, the captain of David's body-guard (2Sa 8:18; 20:23; 23:20,22; 1Ki 1:8, etc.). Jehoiada was "the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel" (2Sa 23:20), but commentators read with Septuagint and…

(Jehovah knows). Father of Benaiah, David’s well-known warrior. (2 Samuel 8:18) 1Kin 1 and 2 passim ; (1 Chronicles 18:17) etc. (B.C. before 1046.) Leader of the Aaronites, i.e. the priests; who joined David at Hebron. (1 Chronicles 12:27) (B.C. 1053-46.)…

jehoiakim.s: je-hoi'-a-kim (yehoyaqim, "Yahweh will establish"; Ioakeim): The name given him by Pharaoh-necoh, who raised him to the throne as vassal king in place of his brother Jehoahaz, is changed from Eliakim (`elyaqim, "God will establish"). The change compounds the…

(whom Jehovah sets up), called Eliakim, son of Josiah and king of Judah. After deposing Jehoahaz, Pharaoh-necho set Eliakim, his elder brother, upon the throne, and changed his name to Jehoiakim, B.C. 608-597. For four years Jehoiakim was subject toi Egypt,…
He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C.
(whom Jehovah sets up), eldest son of Josiah, and the brother and successor of Jehoahaz, king of Judah.

jehoiarib.s: Jehovah defends, a priest at Jerusalem, head of one of the sacerdotal courses (1 Chr. 9:10; 24:7). His “course” went up from Babylon after the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42).
(whom Jehovah defends), head of the first of the twenty-four courses of priests. (1 Chronicles 24:7)
je-hoi'-a-rib (yehoyaribh, "Yahweh pleads" or "contends"): A priest in Jerusalem (1Ch 9:10);
(whom Jehovah defends), the head of the first course of priests. 1 Chr 24:7.

jehonadab.s: Jehovah is liberal; or, whom Jehovah impels. (1.) A son of Shimeah, and nephew of David. It was he who gave the fatal wicked advice to Amnon, the heir to the throne (2 Sam. 13:3-6). He was very “subtil,” but unprincipled. (2.) A son of Rechab, the founder of a…
je-hon'-a-dab (yehonadhabh, either "Yahweh is noble" or "liberal," or "Yahweh has impelled") = Jonadab (yonadhabh, same meaning): (1) Jehonadab in the Hebrew of 2Sa 13:5;
or JONA'DAB(whom Jehovah incites), the son of Rechab, the founder of the Rechabites, which see. He joined Jehu in the slaughter of the Baalites. 2 Kgs 10:15-23.
(whom Jehovah impels) and Jon’adab, the son of Rechab, founder of the Rechabites, an Arab chief.

Whom Jehovah gave. (1.) One of the stewards of David’s store-houses (1 Chr. 27:25). (2.) A Levite who taught the law to the people of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8). (3.) Neh. 12:18.

je-ho'-va nis'-i (yahweh nicci, "Yahweh is my banner"): So Moses named the altar which he reared to signalize the defeat of the Amalekites by Israel under Joshua, at Rephidim (Ex 17:15).
(Jehovah my banner), the name given by Moses to the altar which he built as a memorial of the discomfiture of the Amalekites. Ex 17:15.

jehovah-shalom.s: je-ho'-va sha'-lom (yahweb shalom, "Yahweh is peace"): This was the name given by Gideon to the altar he built at Ophra, in allusion to the word spoken to him by the Lord, "Peace be unto thee" (Jud 6:24). It is equivalent to "Yahweh is well disposed."
Jehovah send peace, the name which Gideon gave to the altar he erected on the spot at Ophrah where the angel appeared to him (Judg. 6:24).
(Jehovah [is] peace), an altar erected by Gideon in Ophrah, where the angel greeted him with "Peace be unto thee!" Jud 6:24.

Jehovah our rightousness, rendered in the Authorized Version, “The LORD our righteousness,” a title given to the Messiah (Jer. 23:6, marg.), and also to Jerusalem (33:16, marg.).

je-hoz'-a-bad (yehozabhadh, "Yahweh has bestowed"): (1) A servant of King Jehoash of Judah.

jehozadak.s: Jehovah-justified, the son of the high priest Seraiah at the time of the Babylonian exile (1 Chr. 6:14, 15). He was carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar, and probably died in Babylon. He was the father of Jeshua, or Joshua, who returned with Zerubbabel.

(Jehovah justifies), usually called Jozadak or Josedech. He was the son of the high priest Seraiah. (1 Chronicles 6:14,15) When his father was slain at Riblah by order of Nebuchadnezzar, (2 Kings 25:18,21) Jehozadak was led away captive to Babylon. (1…

(whom God makes just), the son of the high priest Seraiah, who was murdered at Riblah by Nebuchadnezzar.

je-hu'-kal (yechukhal, probably meaning "Yahweh is able"): A courtier sent by King Zedekiah to Jeremiah to ask the prophet to pray for the king and the people (Jer 37:3). Most versions except Septuagint, with Jer 38:1, have "Jucal" ( yukhal, same meaning).
or JU'CAL (potent), one of those whom Zedekiah the king sent to Jeremiah the prophet, and who afterward asked for the latter's death. Jer 37:3; Isa 38:1.

jehudi.s: (a Jew), son of Nethaniah, a man employed by the princes of Jehoiakim’s court to fetch Baruch to read Jeremiah’s denunciation, (Jeremiah 36:14) and then by the king to fetch the volume itself and read it to him. vs. (Jeremiah 36:21,23) (B.C. 605.)

A Jew, son of Nethaniah. He was sent by the princes to invite Baruch to read Jeremiah’s roll to them (Jer. 36:14, 21).
je-hu'-di (yehudhi, properly "a Jew"): An officer of King Jehoiakim (Jer 36:14,21,23).

jeiel.s: Snatched away by God. (1.) A descendant of Benjamin (1 Chr. 9:35; 8:29). (2.) One of the Levites who took part in praising God on the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:5). (3.) 2 Chr. 29:13. A Levite of the sons of Asaph. (4.) 2 Chr. 26:11. A scribe.…

(dove), the eldest of Job's three daughters, born after his recovery. Job 42:14.

jeremiah.s: Raised up or appointed by Jehovah. (1.) A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:10). (2.) A Gadite warrior (1 Chr. 12:13). (3.) A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4). (4.) One of the chiefs of the tribe of Manasseh on the…

Contender with Baal; or, let Baal plead, a surname of Gideon; a name given to him because he destroyed the altar of Baal (Judg. 6:32; 7:1; 8:29; 1 Sam. 12:11).

jerubbesheth.s: jer-ub-be'-sheth, je-rub'-e-sheth (yerubbesheth, see JERUBBAAL, for meaning): It is found once (2Sa 11:21) for JERUBBAAL.
Contender with the shame; i.e., idol, a surname also of Gideon (2 Sam. 11:21).
(contender with the shame), a name of Gideon. (2 Samuel 11:21)

jeruel.s: Founded by God, a “desert” on the ascent from the valley of the Dead Sea towards Jerusalem. It lay beyond the wilderness of Tekoa, in the direction of Engedi (2 Chr. 20:16, 20). It corresponds with the tract of country now called el-Hasasah.

(founded by God), The wilderness of, the place in which Jehoshaphat was informed by Jahaziel the Levite that he should encounter the hordes of Ammon, Moab and the Mehunims. (2 Chronicles 20:16) The name has not been met with.

(founded of God), THE WIL'DERNESS OF, the place in which Jehoshaphat met and defeated the Ammonites, Moabites, and their allies.

or JERU'SHAH (possessed), the mother of Jotham, king of Judah. 2 Kgs 15:33; 2 Chr 27:1.
(possessed), daughter of Zadok and queen of Uzziah. (2 Kings 15:33) (B.C. 806.)

jeshaiah.s: Deliverance of Jehovah. (1.) A Kohathite Levite, the father of Joram, of the family of Eliezer (1 Chr. 26:25); called also Isshiah (24:21). (2.) One of the sons of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 15). (3.) One of the three sons of Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:21). (4.) Son of…

jeshanah.s: a town which, with its dependent villages, was one of the three taken from Jeroboam by Abijah, 2 Chr 13:19, and identified by Swartz with al-Samin, 2 miles west of Bethel; but this requires confirmation.
jesh'-a-na, je-sha'-na (yeshanah): A town named with Bethel and Ephron among the places taken by Abijah from Jeroboam (2Ch 13:19).
(old), a town which, with its dependent villages, was one of the three taken from Jeroboam by Abijah. (2 Chronicles 13:19)
A city of the kingdom of Israel (2 Chr. 13:19).

jesharelah.s: jesh-a-re'-la (yesar'elah, meaning doubtful): One of the (or probably a family of) Levitical musicians (1Ch 25:14), called "Asharelah" in verse 2. The names should be written "Asarelah" and "Jesarelah."
(right before God), son of Asaph, and head of the seventh of the twenty-four wards into which the musicians of the Levites were divided. (1 Chronicles 25:14) [Asarelah] (B.C. 1014).
(right toward God), the head of the seventh division of the Levite musicians. 1 Chr 25:14. In 1 Chr 25:2 he is called Asarelah.
Upright towards God, the head of the seventh division of Levitical musicians (1 Chr. 25:14).

jeshebeab.s: (father’s seat), head of the fourteenth course of priests. (1 Chronicles 24:13) [Jehoiarib]
(seat of one's father), the chief of the fourteenth division of the priests. 1 Chr 24:13.
je-sheb'-e-ab (yeshebh'abh, meaning uncertain): A Levite of the 14th course (1Ch 24:13).
Seat of his father, the head of the fourteenth division of priests (1 Chr. 24:13).

jesher.s: (uprightness), one of the sons of Caleb the son of Hezron by his wife Azubah. (1 Chronicles 2:18) (B.C. before 1491).

je'-sher (yesher, or yesher, "uprightness"): A son of Caleb (1Ch 2:18).
(uprightness), one of the sons of Caleb, the son of Hezron. 1 Chr 2:18.

jesh'-u-a, je-shu'-a (yeshua`): A place occupied by the children of Judah after their return from captivity (Ne 11:26), evidently, from the places named with it, in the extreme South of Judah.

(gathered by the people), a city of Ephraim, given with its suburbs to a Kohathite Levites.

(possessed by the people), a city of the tribe of Zebulun, allotted with its suburbs to the Merarite Levites. (Joshua 21:34) Its modern site is Tell Kaimon, an eminence which stands just below the eastern termination of Carmel.
jok'-ne-am (yoqne`am): A royal city of the Canaanites taken by Joshua and described as "in Carmel" (Jos 12:22), in the territory of Zebulun, and allotted to the Merarite Levites (21:34).

jokshan.s: jok'-shan (yoqshan, meaning unknown): Son of Abraham and Keturah (Ge 25:2,3 parallel 1Ch 1:32). Tuch suggested that yoqshan = yoqTan (Ge 10:25-29); see HDB, under the word; Skinner, Gen, 350.

Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).
(a folder), the son of Abraham by Keturah. Gen 25:2-3; 1 Chr 1:32.

jok'-tan (yoqTan, meaning unknown): "Son" of Eber, and "father" of 13 tribes (Ge 10:25,26,29; 1Ch 1:19,20,23).
(who is made small), a descendant of Shem, ancestor of the Joktanite Arabs. Gen 10:25-30; 1 Chr 1:19-23.

jonah, book of.s: This book professes to give an account of what actually took place in the experience of the prophet.

jonas.s: (1.) Greek form of Jonah (Matt. 12:39, 40, 41, etc.). (2.) The father of the apostles Peter (John 21:15-17) and Andrew; but the reading should be (also in 1:42), as in the Revised Version, “John,” instead of Jonas.

Whom Jehovah gave, the name of fifteen or more persons that are mentioned in Scripture.

=Jeho’ram. (1.) One of the kings of Israel (2 Kings 8:16, 25, 28). He was the son of Ahab. (2.) Jehoram, the son and successor of Jehoshaphat on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 8:24).

(the descender), the great river of Palestine, as the Nile is of Egypt.

jubilee.s: A joyful shout or clangour of trumpets, the name of the great semi-centennial festival of the Hebrews.

jahdiel.s: (whom Jehovah makes joyful), a chieftain of Manasseh on the east of Jordan. (1 Chronicles 5:24) (B.C. 320.)

jehush.s: (to whom God hastens), son of eshek, a remote descendant of Saul. (1 Chronicles 8:39)
(a collector), one of Saul's descendants. 1 Chr 8:39.

(who gathers the people), a Levite in David's time. 1 Chr 23:19 ;1 Chr 24:23

jekamiah.s: jek-am-mi'-a (yeqamyah, "may Yahweh establish"): (1) A Judahite, son of Shallum (1Ch 2:41). (2) A son of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin); in the King James Version "Jecamiah" (1Ch 3:18).
(whom Jehovah gathers), son of Shallum, in the line of Ahlai. (1 Chronicles 2:41) (B.C. about 588.)
(whom Jehovah gathers), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:18.

jekuthiel.s: je-ku'-thi-el (yeqthi'el meaning doubtful): A Judahite (1Ch 4:18). The meaning may be "preservation of God" or perhaps the same as yoqthe'el, "Joktheel," the name of a place in Jos 15:38; 2Ki 14:7.
a man recorded in the genealogies of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:18)
(piety toward God), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:18.

jemimah.s: je-mi'-ma (yemimah, perhaps a diminutive meaning "little dove"): The first daughter of Job (42:14), born after his restoration from affliction.

jemnaan.s: jem'-na-an (Iemnaan): A city on the coast of Palestine; mentioned among those affected by the expedition of Holofernes (Judith 2:28; 3:1 ff). The name is used for Jabniel, generally called "Jamnia" by the Greek writers.

(day of God), the eldest son of Simeon. (Genesis 46:10; Exodus 6:15) (B.C. 1706.)

jerechu; jerechus.s: jer'-e-ku, jer'-e-kus the King James Version (1 Esdras 5:22). See JERICHO.

(descent). 1. 1 Chr 1:2. See Jared. 2. A descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:18.

je-sim'-i-el (yesimi'el, "God establishes"): A prince of Simeon (1Ch 4:36).

jezaniah.s: (whom Jehovah hears), the son of Hoshaiah the Maachathite, and one of the captains of the forces who had escaped from Jerusalem during the final attack of the beleaguering army of the Chaldeans.

jezoar.s: (whiteness), the son of Helah, one of the wives of Asher. (1 Chronicles 4:7)
(shining), one of the tribe of Judah. 1 Chr 4:7.

jezrahiah.s: (produced by Jehovah), a Levite, the leader of the choristers at the solemn dedication of the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 12:42) (B.C. 446.)

jidlaph.s: jid'-laf (yidhlaph perhaps "he weeps"): A "son" of Nahor (Ge 22:22).

(rest), a town on the north-east borders of Ephraim. Josh 16:6-7. At Yanus, about 8 miles south-east of Nablus, are extensive ruins, entire houses and walls, covered with immense heaps of earth, and these are identified as the site of Janohah.

jashubilehem.s: (turner back for food), a person or a place named among the descendants of Shelah, the son of Judah by Bath-shua the Canaanitess. (1 Chronicles 4:22)
(turner back for food), either a person or a place mentioned in the genealogical list of Judah. 1 Chr 4:22.

jeaterai.s: (whom Jehovah leads), a Gershonite Levite, 1 Chr 6:21; called Ethni in 1 Chr 6:41.
(whom Jehovah leads), a Gershonite Levite, son of Zerah. (1 Chronicles 6:21)

jeberachiah.s: (whom Jehovah blesses), the father of the Zechariah whom Isaiah took as a witness. Isa 8:2.

jebusi.s: (from Jebus), the name employed for the city of Jebus. (Joshua 15:8; 18:16,28)
Josh 15:8; Josh 18:16, Josh 18:28. A name for Jebus. See Jebus and Jerusalem.

jehalelel.s: (who praises God), a Merarite Levite, father of Azariah. (2 Chronicles 29:12)

jehezekel.s: (whom God makes strong), a priest to whom was given by David the charge of the twentieth of the twenty-four courses in the service of the house of Jehovah. (1 Chronicles 24:16) (B.C. 1014.)
(whom God makes strong), the head of the twentieth priestly course, 1 Chr 24:16; same name as Ezekiel.

jehieli.s: (a Jehielite), according to the Authorized Version a Gershonite Levite of the family of Laadan. (1 Chronicles 26:21,22)
a patronymic; the descendants of Jehiel. 1 Chr 26:21-22; comp. 1 Chr 23:8; 1 Chr 29:8.

jehoadah.s: (whom Jehovah adorns), one of the descendants of Saul, 1 Chr 8:36; in 1 Chr 9:42 called Jarah.
(whom Jehovah adorns), one of the descendants of Saul. (1 Chronicles 8:36)

jekabzeel.s: (which God gathers), a place in the southern part of Judah, Neh 11:25; also called Kabzeel (God's gathering*), Josh 15:21; 2 Sam 23:20.
(what God gathers), a fuller form of the name of Kabzeel, the most remote city of Judah on the southern frontier. (Nehemiah 11:25)

jephthae.s: (whom God sets free), (Hebrews 11:32) the Greek form of the name Jephthah.
the Greek form of Jephthah. Heb 11:32.

jeremie, the epistle of.s: is the title of a pretended letter from the prophet Jeremiah appended to the Apocryphal book of Baruch.

jerub-baal.s: (with whom Baal contends), Jud 6:32, and JERUB'BESHETH (with whom the idol contends). 2 Sam 11:21. See Gideon.

jesaiah.s: (salvation of Jehovah). Son of Hananiah, brother of Pelatiah and grandson of Zerubbabel. (1 Chronicles 3:21) (B.C. after 536.)
(saving). 1. One of David's posterity. 1 Chr 3:21. 2. A Benjamite. Neh 11:7.

jesus, son of sirach, book of.t: Jesus, Son Of Sirach, Book Of

jewels.s: This term is applied to ornaments made of the precious metals and used to adorn the person.

jimna.s: (prosperity), the first-born of Asher. (Numbers 26:44) He is elsewhere called in the Authorized Version Jimnah, (Genesis 46:17) and Imnah. (1 Chronicles 7:30)
or JIM'NAH (good fortune), the eldest son of Asher. Gen 46:17; Num 26:44. He is also called Imnah in 1 Chr 7:30. His descendants are the Jimnites. Num 26:44.

jiphthah-el.s: (God opens),the name of a valley forming one of the landmarks for the boundary of Zebulun and Asher.

jonath-elem - rechokim.s: (a dumb dove of distant places), part of the title to Ps. 56; not found elsewhere in the Bible. Most likely it was the name of some popular melody to which tune the Psalm was to be sung.

jorkoam.s: (paleness of the people), either a descendant of Caleb the son of Hezron, or the name of a place in the tribe of Judah. (1 Chronicles 2:44)
(paleness of the people), probably the name of a person; but if a place, it is a town in the territory of Judah. 1 Chr 2:44.

josedech.s: (whom Jehovah makes just). Hag 1:1. See Jehozadak, Jozadak.

josheb-bassebet.s: (he loho sits in the seat), in the margin of 2 Sam 23:8. See Jashobeam.

josibiah.s: (to whom God gives a dwelling), the father of Jehu, a Simeonite. (1 Chronicles 4:35)
(whom Jehovah lets dwell), a Siraeonite chief. 1 Chr 4:35.

jotbath.s: or JOT BATHAH (goodness, pleasantness), a station of the Hebrews in the desert, Num 33:33, and on the west side of the Arabah, "a land of rivers of waters." Deut 10:7.

jumbal.s: (music), a son of Lamech, and the inventor of the harp and organ. Gen 4:21.

jubilee, year of.s: came at the close of seven weeks of years, or eveiy fiftieth year, so that two sabbatical years came together.

judaea, or judea, province of.s: a name applied to that part of Canaan occupied by those who returned after the Assyrian and Babylonian captivities.

judaea, the hill-country of.s: the central ridge of mountains stretching from north to south, and forming as it were the backbone of the land of Palestine. Luke 1:65.

judah, the kingdom of.s: Extent. — The kingdom of Judah embraced not only the territory of the tribe of Judah (see above), but also included the larger part of Benjamin on the north-east, Dan on the north-west, and Simeon on the south. The area thus under the dominion of Judah is…

judah, the city of.s: 2 Chr 25:28. Several manuscripts, and all the versions except the Chaldee, read "city of David," which was a name of Mount Zion at Jerusalem, where were the tombs of the kings.

judgment, judgments.s: These are words of frequent occurrence in the sacred Scriptures, and the sense of them is generally determined by the connection.

judgment-hall.s: a room or office in the palace of the Roman governor where causes were tried and justice administered, John 18:28.

judith, the apocryphal book of.s: one of the earliest specimens of historical fiction, relates the brave action of Judith, a Jewish widow distinguished for her beauty, her virtue, and her patriotism.

jaareoregim.s: (forests of the weavers), (2 Samuel 21:19) a Bethlehemite, and the father of Elhanan who slew Goliath. In the parallel passage, (1 Chronicles 20:5) Jair is found instead of Jaare, and Oregim is omitted. (B.C. 1063.)

jaazer, or jazer.s: (Jehovah helps), a town on the east of Jordan, in or near to Gilead. (Numbers 32:1,3; 1 Chronicles 26:31) We first hear of it in possession of the Amorites, and as taken by Israel after Heshbon, and on their way from thence to Bashan. (Numbers 21:32) It seems…

jahaz, also jahaza, jahazah and juhzah.s: (trodden down). Under these four forms is given in the Authorized Version the name of a place which in the Hebrew appears as Yahats and Yahtsah . At Jahaz the decisive battle was fought between the children of Israel and Sihon king of the Amorites. (Numbers…

jahaza.s: (trodden down). (Joshua 13:18) [Jahaz, Also Jahaza, Jahazah And Juhzah]

jahazah.s: (trodden down). (Joshua 21:36; Jeremiah 48:21) [Jahaz, Also Jahaza, Jahazah And Juhzah]

jahnziah.s: (whom Jehovah watches over), son of Tikvah, apparently a priest. (Ezra 10:15)

jakamean.s: (who gathers the people together), a Levite in the time of King David; fourth of the sons of Hebron, the son of Kohath. (1 Chronicles 23:19; 24:23) (B.C. 1014.)

james the less.s: called the Less because younger or smaller in stature than James the son of Zebedee.

japhleli.s: (the Japhletite). The boundary of the “Japhletite” is one of the landmarks on the south boundary line of Ephraim. (Joshua 16:3)

jegarsahadutha.s: (heap of testimony), the Aramaean name given by Laban the Syrian to the heap of stones which he erected as a memorial of the compact between Jacob and himself.

jehoshuah.s: in the genealogy of Ephraim. (1 Chronicles 7:27)

jehovahjireh.s: (Jehovah will see or provide), the name given by Abraham to the place on which he had been commanded to offer Isaac, to commemorate the interposition of the angel of Jehovah, who appeared to prevent the sacrifice, (Genesis 22:14) and provided another victim.

jehovahnissi.s: (Jehovah my banner), the name given by Moses to the altar which he built in commemoration of the discomfiture of the Amalekites. (Exodus 17:15)

jehovahshalom.s: (Jehovah (is) peace), or, with an ellipsis, “Jehovah the God of peace.” The altar erected by Gideon in Orphrah was so called in memory of the salutation addressed to him by the angel of Jehovah, “Peace be unto thee.” (Judges 6:24)

jerahmeelites.s: (descendants of Jerahmeel), The, the tribe descended from the first of the foregoing persons. (1 Samuel 27:10) They dwelt in the south of Judah.

jerubbaal, or jerubbaal.s: (contender with Baal), the surname of Gideon, which he acquired in consequence of destroying the altar of Baal, when his father defended him from the vengeance of the Abiezrites. (Judges 6:32)

jerushah.s: (possessed). (2 Chronicles 27:1) The same as the preceding.

jeshuah.s: a priest in the reign of David, (1 Chronicles 24:11) the same as Jeshua, No. 2. (B.C. 1014.)

jewish.s: of or belonging to Jews; an epithet applied to their rabbinical legends. (Titus 1:14)

jinah.s: (lamentation), a city of Judah, on the extreme south boundary of the tribe, next to Edom. (Joshua 15:22)

jirjathaim.s: (the two cities). On the east of the Jordan, one of the places which were taken possession of and rebuilt by the Reubenites, and had fresh names conferred on them, (Numbers 32:37) and see (Numbers 32:38) the first and last of which are known with some…

joaada.s: (whom Jehovah favors), high priest after his father Eliashib. (Nehemiah 13:28) (B.C. after 446.)

john the apostle.s: was the son of Zebedee, a fisherman on the Lake of Galilee, and of Salome, and brother of James, also an apostle.

john, the first epistle general of.t: John, The First Epistle General Of
john, the first epistle general of.s: There can be no doubt that the apostle John was the author of this epistle. jokdean.s: (possessed by the people), a city of Judah, in the mountains, (Joshua 15:56) apparently south of Hebron.

jonathelemrechokim.s: (a dumb love of (in) distant places), a phrase found once only in the Bible, as a heading to the 56th psalm.

joppa, or japho.s: (beauty), now Jaffa, a town on the southwest coast of Palestine, in the portion of Dan.

josedech = jehozadak.s: (whom Jehovah makes just), the son of Seraiah. (Haggai 1:1,12,14; 2:2,4; Zechariah 6:11)

jotbath, or jotbathah.s: (goodness), (10:7; Numbers 33:33) a desert station of the Israelites.

jubilee, the year of.s: the name.—The name jubilee is derived from the Hebrew jobel, the joyful shout or clangor of trumpets, by which the year of jubilee was announced.

judaea, or judea.s: (from Judah), a territorial division which succeeded to the overthrow of the ancient landmarks of the tribes of Israel and Judah in their respective captivities.

judas, the lords brother.s: Among the brethren of our Lord mentioned by the people of Nazareth. (Matthew 13:55; Mark 6:3) Whether this and the Jude above are the same is still a disputed point.

jude, or judas.s: called also LEBBEUS and Thaddeus, Authorized Version “Judas the brother of James,” one of the twelve apostles.

judges.s: The judges were temporary and special deliverers, sent by God to deliver the Israelites from their oppressors;

judith, the book of.s: one of the books of the Apocrypha, belongs to the earliest specimens of historical fiction. As to its authorship it belongs to the Maccabean period, B.C. 175-135, which it reflects not only in its general spirit, but even in its smaller traits.

junias.s: Revised Version for Junia above. It is the more literal form.

jushabhesed.s: (whose love is returned), son of Zerubbabel. (1 Chronicles 3:20)
